full-title: The Temples of Angkor: Temples Buried in the Jungle
quote: Cambodia is a destination whose fame is linked to an unmissable site: Angkor. Renowned for its majestic temples, this emblematic place attracts visitors from all over the world, seduced by the beauty of its monuments. A magical place steeped in history, making this site one of the treasures of Southeast Asia.
introduction: Below you will find a complete guide to our visit of the Angkor temples. Which temples to visit and how to organize your stay?
google-description: From the majestic Angkor Wat to the mysterious Ta Prohm, via the impressive faces of the Bayon and the more confidential temples, each site has its own atmosphere and reserves its share of discoveries. We take you with us to explore the Angkor temples. Our travel story with photos, tips and tricks.
social-network-description: From the majestic Angkor Wat to the mysterious Ta Prohm, via the impressive faces of the Bayon and the more confidential temples, each site has its own atmosphere and reserves its share of discoveries.

where.title: Where?
where.part1: Angkor is located in northwestern Cambodia about #5 to 6 km north of Siem Reap city center#, and about 315 km from Phnom Penh.

when.title: When?
when.part1: Most temples are accessible #from 7:30 AM to 6:30 PM#, while some open their doors as early as 5 AM.
when.part2: These hours allow visitors to admire the temples at sunrise and sunset. An exceptional light then envelops the Angkor temples.

how.title: How to get there and how to get around on site?
how.part1: Given the size of the site, it is essential to plan a means of transport to explore its many temples but also to get there. Several options are available to you, depending on your budget, your desires and your way of traveling:
how.part2: #Bicycle#: shop in Siem Reap - about $5 per day for a basic bike, about $10 for a mountain bike, about $25 for an electric bike.
how.part3: #Tuk-tuk#: rental directly on site or via your hotel - about $25 per day depending on the route.
how.part4: #Car with driver#: to be booked in advance online - about $50 per day.
how.part5: The simplest and most comfortable options are especially tuk-tuks and taxis.
how.part6: You thus enjoy a visit at your own pace, freely choosing the temples you wish to discover. Your driver accompanies you throughout the day and waits for you at each stage, for the duration of your visits.
how.part7: However, to reach the most distant temples, you will need to opt for a car with driver, the distances being too great for a tuk-tuk journey.
how.part8: We had booked a private driver on the website: [Angkor taxi private](https://angkortaxiprivate.com/Siem-Reap-Driver/Carmary-Car-4-seat-2-Days.html).

how-long.title: How long?
how-long.part1: This is the first question you should ask yourself before planning your visit of the site as it will allow you to best organize your visit.
how-long.part2: Several pass formulas are offered: #1, 3 or 7 days#, depending on your desires and the time you have available.
how-long.part3: #The 1-day pass# is the one we advise against the most, it will limit you greatly and you will only be able to visit the closest temples, therefore inevitably the most visited ones.
how-long.part4: #The 3-day pass# is particularly interesting since it is valid for a period of one week from its purchase date, the visit days do not necessarily have to be consecutive. Three days is, in our opinion, the best compromise to explore the must-see temples, but also take the time to discover less frequented sites without getting too bored.
how-long.part5: #The 7-day pass#, for its part, is valid for 30 days from its purchase date, which leaves a huge amount of time to organize and alternate temple visits and other discoveries. However, from our point of view, 7 days to visit the temples risks being a bit excessive and is really not necessary to visit all the temples.

what-time-of-year.title: At what time of year?
what-time-of-year.part1: The best period to visit [Cambodia](cambodia) is between November and March.
what-time-of-year.part2: The climate in Cambodia is marked by the monsoon. The year is therefore divided into a dry season and a rainy season.
what-time-of-year.part3: #From November to March#, it's the dry season, warm but not excessive temperature, very little rain and low humidity. However, lots of people.
what-time-of-year.part4: #From April to October#, it's the rainy season, it doesn't necessarily rain every day but there are more risks of heavy showers, it's much more muggy and there is also more humidity.
what-time-of-year.part5: On our side, we went in April.

how-much.title: Price
how-much.part1: Entry to the park is via an #Angkor Pass#.
how-much.part5: The pass is purchased at the official ticket office (Angkor Ticket Center), located on Route 60.
how-much.part6: You can now buy your tickets online on the [official website](https://www.angkorenterprise.gov.kh/en/available-tickets?tab=temples).

where-to-stay.title: Where to stay?
where-to-stay.part1: There is no accommodation inside the site, so you will necessarily need to find somewhere to sleep mainly in #Siem Reap#.
where-to-stay.part2: Youth hostels, guesthouses and hotels, you will find everything and at all prices.
where-to-stay.part3: We advise you to take a hotel not too far from the city center to enjoy and go out in the evening. A fairly comfortable hotel with a restaurant not too far away if possible too because after days of temple visits I guarantee you will be tired!
where-to-stay.part4: Prices vary enormously depending on the seasons.
where-to-stay.part5: You can compare offers yourself on [Booking](booking-search:Siem Reap).

what-to-bring.title: What to put in your bag?
what-to-bring.part1: Remember to bring #light and comfortable clothing#, adapted to the heat. Prefer outfits covering shoulders and knees to visit the temples and respect the places, but also to protect yourself from mosquitoes.
what-to-bring.part2: Don't forget your #raincoat or poncho#, as showers are frequent and good #hiking shoes#.
what-to-bring.part4: A sunscreen with a high protection index.
what-to-bring.part5: A hat or cap to protect you from the sun.
what-to-bring.part7: A water bottle to stay well hydrated throughout the day.

itinerary.title: Our itinerary
itinerary.part1: To facilitate your discovery and guide you at best, #two circuits# are proposed.
itinerary.part2: If you book a tuk-tuk or a private taxi, the drivers are used to it and know the circuit routes by heart. You will just have to tell them which circuit you want to do that day and they will guide you from temple to temple, a real time saver!
itinerary.part3: We've put #the small circuit in purple and the grand circuit in red#.
itinerary.part4: We did the small circuit on the first day and the grand circuit on the second day.
itinerary.part5: For the third day, we went to another temple, outside the site, which was on the way to the [floating village of Kampong Phluk](kampong-phluk).

visit.title: THE TEMPLES OF ANGKOR
visit.part1: Angkor has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1992.
visit.part2: Angkor is not limited to a single temple: it is an immense #archaeological zone of over 400 km²#.
visit.part3: Throughout the visit you will see temples, vestiges, basins and ruins invaded by the jungle. Linger on the inscriptions and the superb details engraved on the temples, these details bring the stone to life.
visit.part4: #A hot air balloon flight# allows you to gain some height and admire the temples from a different angle, enjoy it if you have the time.

visit1.title: ANGKOR WAT, THE KINGDOM OF THE GODS
visit1.part1: When one evokes the temples of Angkor, a name immediately comes to mind: #Angkor Wat or Angkor Vat#. And if the name doesn't ring a bell, its silhouette certainly will. #True emblem and pride of Cambodia#, it is the main image used to illustrate the country on postcards or guides. It even figures at the center of their national flag.
visit1.part2: #Angkor Wat is the largest temple of the Angkor site#. It is surrounded by immense moats and to access it, one takes a long avenue leading to the heart of the temple.
visit1.part3: From afar it amazes with its five majestic towers, up close it impresses with its superb sculptures representing gods, men, animals and scenes from Khmer mythology.
visit1.part4: Unlike many other temples of the site, it is remarkably well preserved. According to researchers, nearly #300,000 workers and 6,000 elephants# would have been mobilized for its construction.
visit1.part5: #The sunrise over Angkor Wat# is undoubtedly one of the most magical moments of the visit. From the first glimmers of dawn, the five towers of the temple outline themselves in the sky and reflect in the moats and basins located in front of the monument.
visit1.part6: A grandiose spectacle, become one of the emblematic images of Cambodia.

visit2.title: ANGKOR THOM, THE GATE OF THE CITY
visit2.part1: Access to Angkor Thom is via #five monumental gates#.
visit2.part2: The South Gate is the most famous and best preserved of the five entrances. It is accessible via a stone bridge lined with immense statues. About 23 meters high, this imposing gate is distinguished by #its four sculpted faces#, turned towards the four cardinal points.
visit2.part3: Surrounded by moats and protected by a 12 km wall, Angkor Thom is an ancient city grouping several monuments, including the famous Bayon temple.

visit3.title: BAYON, THE TEMPLE OF A THOUSAND FACES
visit3.part1: The Bayon temple is located at the very heart of the city of Angkor Thom.
visit3.part2: #Famous for its imposing towers adorned with giant faces with mysterious expressions#.
visit3.part3: Originally, there were 54 towers, but only a few are still relatively intact today. They bear #more than 200 faces sculpted in stone#, whose smiling faces seem to observe you from all sides when approaching the temple.
visit3.part4: Abandoned in the 15th century, the Bayon temple was gradually invaded by vegetation. It remained long forgotten before being rediscovered by European archaeologists several centuries later. Restoration work was then undertaken to give it its current appearance.
visit3.part5: Around the Bayon, several monuments are also worth a visit, notably the #Terrace of the Elephants#, nearly 300 meters long, the #Terrace of the Leper King#, famous for its sculpted walls, as well as the #Baphuon# temple.

visit4.title: THOMMANON AND CHAU SAY TEVODA
visit4.part1: Thommanon and Chau Say Tevoda are two small Khmer temples. Facing each other, they are often nicknamed the "#twin temples#" of Angkor.
visit4.part2: The Thommanon temple is remarkably well preserved, while Chau Say Tevoda has undergone significant restoration work.

visit5.title: TA KEO, THE SACRED MOUNTAIN
visit5.part1: This temple is distinguished by its unfinished appearance, the reasons for which remain unknown, and by its very sober decoration.
visit5.part2: To reach the summit, you must #climb a particularly steep stone staircase#. The climb can be impressive, the descent just as much, especially if you have vertigo, but the effort is worth it. Once at the top, you enjoy a #spectacular view#.
visit5.part3: At the summit stands a central tower, surrounded by four smaller towers.

visit6.title: TA PHROM, ENTWINED BY NATURE
visit6.part1: #Ta Prohm is one of the most emblematic temples of Angkor#.
visit6.part2: World-famous for its emblematic image, where vegetation, over the centuries, has progressively reclaimed its rights.
visit6.part3: Immense trees grow in the middle of the ruins, while #their giant roots wrap around the walls#, cover the roofs and intertwine with the stones. This spectacular encounter between nature and ancient vestiges gives the temple a #mysterious and almost unreal atmosphere#, as if the jungle had gradually engulfed the monument.
visit6.part4: Ta Prohm acquired international fame thanks to the #film Tomb Raider# (2001), with Angelina Jolie, several scenes of which were shot in the temple. Since then, it is often nicknamed the "Tomb Raider temple".
visit6.part5: To prevent the collapse of certain parts of the temple, metal structures have been installed to consolidate the most fragile areas. These developments allow the monument to be preserved while maintaining its wild appearance, which today makes all its charm.

visit7.title: PREAH KHAN, THE TEMPLE OF A THOUSAND CORRIDORS
visit7.part1: The name Preah Khan would translate as "#sacred sword#". According to legend, a sacred sword was once kept in this place. Today, a replica of this sword is displayed at the Royal Palace of [Phnom Penh](todo).
visit7.part2: Preah Khan is distinguished by its maze of interior courtyards and corridors. Between its colossal columns and #its thousand corridors#, the temple seems immense.
visit7.part3: Here too nature has somewhat reclaimed its rights, which gives the temple magnificent landscapes.

visit8.title: NEAK POAN, THE TEMPLE OF WATER
visit8.part1: Access to Neak Pean, nicknamed the "#temple of water#", is via a long walkway of several hundred meters crossing a vast basin dotted with lotus flowers.
visit8.part2: The temple itself may seem quite modest but its path through the water gives it a peaceful moment thanks to the natural setting surrounding it.

visit9.title: TA SOM, THE TEMPLE OF ENTWINED ROOTS
visit9.part1: The gate of Ta Som, majestically #framed by the roots of a tree#, offers one of the most photogenic panoramas of Angkor.
visit9.part2: One discovers magnificent sculptures on the walls surrounding it, lush vegetation enveloping the site and giving it a particularly peaceful atmosphere.
visit9.part3: This very small temple really has a lot of charm.

visit10.title: EASTERN MEBON, THE TEMPLE OF ELEPHANTS
visit10.part1: Built on a small artificial island, at the heart of the immense Eastern Baray reservoir, the temple was once accessible only by boat.
visit10.part2: At the four corners of the first and second levels, #imposing statues of elephants and lions, nearly two meters high#, seem to watch over the temple. Remarkably preserved, they are among the most emblematic elements of the site.

visit11.title: PRE RUP, THE KINGDOM OF RED STONE
visit11.part1: Pre Rup is characterized by #its imposing brick pyramid#, which rises on several levels, with five sanctuaries at its summit. From its summit, the panoramic view offers a magnificent viewpoint.
visit11.part2: In late afternoon, #the sunlight sublimates the red/orange colored bricks# and gives the site a very particular charm.

visit12.title: BANTEAY KDEI
visit12.part1: Banteay Kdei seduces with its mysterious atmosphere, #sublimated by the presence of majestic century-old trees# whose imposing roots seem to embrace the temple's vestiges.
visit12.part2: The current state of degradation of Banteay Kdei is explained in large part by the materials used during its construction and by the impressive roots of the trees.

visit13.title: PRASAT KRAVAN, THE SANCTUARY OF RED BRICK
visit13.part1: Unlike most temples of Angkor, the Prasat Kravan temple is distinguished by #its brick construction#, rather than stone.
visit13.part2: Don't hesitate to go inside the towers, you can admire several representations of #the deity Vishnu#.

visit14.title: BAKONG, OUTSIDE THE SITE
visit14.part1: It is the first temple entirely #built in sandstone#, an architectural model that will inspire the construction of the great sanctuaries of Angkor.
visit14.part2: Less frequented than the temples of the main circuit, the site invites a quieter discovery, at its own pace, far from tourist agitation.
visit14.part3: Like most temples, statues of lions and elephants guard the entrances and steps.
visit14.part4: We added it to our circuit because it was on the way to see [the floating village Kampong Phluk](kampong-phluk).
visit14.part5: Some temples do not require a long visit, for some even half an hour is enough but the visit is no less interesting. This also allows varying the pace of the visit day and it feels good too.
visit14.part6: Whatever your route, you cannot help but be seduced by these majestic vestiges, gradually reconquered by nature.
visit14.part7: Each temple has its own identity, its architecture and its particularities.

conclusion: Angkor is a place that is not limited to a few must-see temples: it is discovered, explored and savored over the visits. A true journey through time, whose memory is kept for a long time and which inevitably makes you want to return.
